{{Quote|Not to judge a droid by his plating, but one look at their paint jobs, and you know they're nothing but trouble!|R0-GR writes about R4-I9 and R2-Q5|<ref name="Droidography" />}}
'''R4-I9''' was an [[R4 astromech droid|R4 astromech]] [[Astromech droid|droid]]<ref name="Metal Figure Collection" /> with [[Gender|masculine]] programming,<ref name="Droidography" /> dark [[Color|blue]] panelling and a black [[sensor]] who served the [[Galactic Empire]]. In the [[Imperial Era|era]] of the [[Galactic Civil War]], the [[astromech droid]] was deployed in the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|first Death Star]], patrolling limited areas inside the [[battle station]] and performing [[computer]] maintenance or repair automatically.<ref name="Droid Collection">{{BandaiCite|set=Droid Collection|pack=R4-I9|url=https://bandai-hobby.net/item/01_1890}}</ref> The [[Resistance]] [[droid]] [[R0-GR]] wrote about R4-I9 and his fellow Imperial [[R-series]] droid [[R2-Q5]] in his ''[[Droidography]]'', where he claimed that based on the color of the two Imperial droid's panelling you could tell that they were trouble.<ref name="Droidography" />

{{Droid-stub}}

==Behind the scenes==
In the new ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]], R4-I9 was first pictured on a card in the [[Star Wars Force Attax: The Force Awakens|''2015 Topps Star Wars Force Attax The Force Awakens'']] series of cards released in [[2015]].<ref name="ForceAttax">{{Topps|set=Star Wars Force Attax: The Force Awakens|cardname=Imperial Astromech Droid}}</ref> The droid's name was then provided by the [[2017]] reference book ''[[Star Wars: The Visual Encyclopedia]]'', which was written by [[Adam Bray]], [[Tricia Barr]] and [[Cole Horton]].<ref name="VE" /> the droid originated in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, where it first appeared in the [[1998]] reference book ''[[Star Wars: The Visual Dictionary]]'', which was written by [[David West Reynolds (real person)|David West Reynolds]].<ref name="TVD">''[[Star Wars: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref>
